The small grey book I took from Mary's cupboard turns out to be far more engrossing than I had expected.
I stay up reading through it until the sky outside starts getting dark.
According to the signature on the first page, this book is a collection of Mary's own notes.
A lot of it is completely indecipherable to me - notes written in shorthand or in code, elaborate recipes with no mention as to what they create.
All the same, I find myself eagerly flicking through detailed diagrams of flowers, and descriptions of strange and fascinating ingredients.
Several of the passages are written in diary format, and one section that catches my attention in particular begins about halfway through the notebook.
As Marquis Elerra once wrote, "despite the seemingly endless advance of alchemical principles, a strong heart invariably trumps best practices."
It is something I have observed several times during my work as a doctor.
Patients who strongly wish to recover, and have a clear picture of what recovery will look like for them, will often recover twice as fast as those who don't.
I have even seen people slip from this mortal coil with no cause other than emotional fatigue. The heart has power over the body's shell.
All potions and rituals that I have discovered have a specific, targeted effect, usually based on the properties of the ingredients.
What if I were to develop a concoction that could properly harness the potential of the mind's power over the body?
That could allow someone to reshape their form as they wished?
It would be akin to the discovery of an organic philosopher's stone!
It sounds absurd, I know. But I stand at the precipice of centuries of discovery in the alchemical arts!
The sages in their gleaming towers have made their voices clear - biological alchemy is the realm of madmen.
The practice is meant for "transmutation" and "industry", and nothing more.
But they have no eyes on the ground. What they don't know won't hurt them.
